profile.name: Nick Soto Conde
profile.headline: Mechatronics Engineer
profile.professionalSummary: I am a Mechatronics Engineer working across Big Data, full-stack development, and robotics research. My work spans distributed data platforms, web and mobile applications, and kinematic modeling: connecting data, software, and physical systems through engineering.
profile.location: Lima, Peru (Jesús María) • Available for Remote & Hybrid

about.professionalBackground: My background combines Mechatronics Engineering at UNI and specialized Big Data studies at UTEC with professional experience in data platforms, full-stack development, and robotics research. These three areas connect mathematical modeling, software architecture, and the design of physical systems.
about.engineeringApproach: I solve technical problems using an engineering approach grounded in first principles: integrating mathematical kinematics, robust distributed data processing, and maintainable software architecture. I prioritize building reliable, well-tested, and maintainable systems over fragile complexity.
about.researchInterests: Robotics engineering, lower-limb rehabilitation exoskeletons, forward and inverse kinematic modeling via Denavit–Hartenberg conventions, workspace characterization, and biomedical engineering applications.
about.careerFocus: Building across three engineering areas: reliable data platforms, full-stack software systems, and robotics research and development. I am interested in projects within each area and in the connections between them.

projects.title: 3-DoF Hip Exoskeleton Kinematic Analysis & Workspace Simulation
projects.summary: Direct kinematic characterization and 3D reachable workspace evaluation of a three-degree-of-freedom wearable hip exoskeleton for gait rehabilitation.
projects.problem: Kinematic misalignments between wearable robotic devices and human anatomical hip joints can reduce gait assistance efficacy and cause user discomfort. Precise geometric formulation is essential prior to mechanical manufacturing.
projects.objective: Formulate the kinematic equations using Denavit–Hartenberg parameters and evaluate the 3D reachable workspace envelope to ensure full coverage of physiological walking ranges.
projects.approach: Applied the Denavit–Hartenberg convention to define joint reference frames across sagittal (flexion/extension), frontal (abduction/adduction), and transverse (internal/external rotation) axes. Computational verification was implemented in Python and Wolfram.
projects.architecture: Serial kinematic chain with 3 revolute joints: Joint 1 (Flexion/Extension: -20° to 90°), Joint 2 (Abduction/Adduction: -15° to 45°), and Joint 3 (Internal/External Rotation: -25° to 25°), computing transformation matrix T_0_3 to map the distal cuff.
projects.contributions: Formulated the D-H parameter tables, programmed transformation matrix scripts, generated workspace point clouds, and co-wrote the peer-reviewed conference paper.
projects.challenges: Modeling non-singular joint limits that accurately reflect natural hip ranges of motion without mechanical collisions between exoskeleton links.
projects.results: Kinematic analysis and workspace simulation documented in a CMAAE 2021 conference paper.
projects.evidence: A UTEC CRIS publication record is linked below. The browser model is an illustrative companion; its parameters have not been independently checked against the published model, and it does not establish clinical performance.

projects.title: Financial Data Pipeline Modernization & Cloud Migration
projects.summary: Migration and re-architecture of financial data processes from legacy on-premise infrastructure to AWS Cloud for Santander Consumer Bank.
projects.problem: Legacy on-premise financial workflows had performance bottlenecks, tight coupling to obsolete core systems, and lacked centralized metadata governance across banking domains.
projects.objective: Modernize data processes into domain/subdomain architectures in AWS, re-implement ETL workflows with Apache Spark, and introduce enterprise data governance with DataHub.
projects.approach: Mapped AS-IS processes, designed equivalence models between Core Bancario To-Be vs As-Is, built distributed Spark jobs, orchestrated tasks with AWS Step Functions, and modeled metadata entities in DataHub.
projects.architecture: Amazon S3 Ingestion Layer -> Distributed Data Processing with Apache Spark on AWS EMR & Glue -> Orquestation with AWS Step Functions -> Data Serving (Athena/Redshift) -> Data Governance Catalog in DataHub.
projects.contributions: Created Python/SQL scripts for structured requirement gathering, developed distributed Spark ETLs, established data dictionaries, and integrated metadata governance schemas into DataHub under corporate standards.
projects.challenges: Reconciling historical accounting definitions between disparate banking cores while maintaining strict data consistency and zero regression in financial metrics.
projects.results: Achieved consistent execution of financial data pipelines on AWS, established standardized squad workflows, and streamlined banking core equivalence mappings.
projects.evidence: This case describes my professional experience with Santander Consumer Bank through IDM Technology and SES. Client code, datasets, and deployment records are not published in this portfolio.

projects.title: Mobile & Web Platform with Integrated Predictive Recommendation
projects.summary: Full-stack mobile (Android) and web application integrating REST microservices and a machine learning decision-tree model for product recommendation.
projects.problem: Agricultural distributors and commercial teams needed a reliable, low-latency mobile tool to browse catalogs and receive data-driven category recommendations.
projects.objective: Develop a responsive cross-platform mobile and web application connected to containerized backend APIs serving real-time predictive models.
projects.approach: Built mobile/web clients with React Native / React + TypeScript; developed Flask REST microservices containerized in Docker; trained and embedded a decision tree model for product recommendations.
projects.architecture: React & React Native Client -> REST API Gateway -> Flask Python Microservices -> Scikit-Learn Inference Engine -> Cloud Storage & Database Services on AWS / GCP.
projects.contributions: Planned module routing and component architecture in TypeScript, developed Flask REST APIs, integrated the ML prediction pipeline, coordinated tasks using Scrum, and published the app to Google Play Store.
projects.challenges: Ensuring lightweight API response times when executing inference calls over mobile network latencies and managing cross-platform UI parity.
projects.results: Delivered production mobile app on Google Play Store and web dashboard on AWS, enabling real-time product classification and catalog access.
projects.evidence: This case is based on my work at VE7 Agronegocios. Public app, source-code, and deployment links are not currently included in this portfolio.

projects.title: NASA Human Exploration Rover Mechanical & Telemetry Subsystems
projects.summary: Engineering design, kinematic drivetrain evaluation, and telemetry integration for an extraterrestrial exploration rover prototype.
projects.problem: Designing a human-powered roving vehicle capable of traversing simulated planetary obstacles and collecting scientific samples under strict mass and dimensional constraints.
projects.objective: Develop mechanical drive, suspension, and telemetry subsystems complying with NASA competition guidelines and challenging obstacle courses.
projects.approach: Performed 3D CAD modeling, structural stress evaluations, kinematic drivetrain calculations, and onboard sensor telemetry prototyping within Grupo Tharsis UNI.
projects.architecture: Custom dual-human drivetrain, articulated suspension geometry, quick-folding chassis mechanism, and onboard sensor telemetry module.
projects.contributions: Collaborated on drivetrain mechanics, suspension clearance calculations, physical fabrication, and team telemetry integration for Grupo Tharsis UNI.
projects.challenges: Balancing structural rigidity against vehicle weight limits to prevent mechanical deformation on irregular terrain obstacles.
projects.results: Qualified and represented Peru and UNI in the international NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge (Huntsville, Alabama).
projects.evidence: This case describes my contribution within Grupo Tharsis UNI. Participation records, CAD files, and team photographs are not currently linked in this portfolio.
